title: Generic lisse section fibre and normalized fibre-functor data
statement: Let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] in universe $u$, let $k=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ be its function field, and let $A$ be a normed field in universe $u$. Use the category $\mathrm{Lisse}_A(X)$, the all-continuous coefficient ring $R_{A,X}$, constant scalar actions, and the category $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathrm{cont}}_A(G)$ of finite-dimensional representations with continuous matrix entries from [def-sfb-norm-continuous-monodromy-data]. Internal modules and their morphisms are those of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], over the actual pulled-back coefficient ring [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\Omega/k$ be a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure] in universe $u$, put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(\Omega)$ with its Krull topology, and let $U_\Omega=(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}k)$ be the actual closure object of [def-sfb-field-separable-cech-nerve]. Define $\operatorname{genericMap}(X)=j:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ to be the canonical map from the spectrum of the stalk at the generic point, $\operatorname{genericModule}(L)=j^*L$ using the existing inverse image of internal coefficient modules, and $\operatorname{geometricSections}(L)=(j^*L)(U_\Omega)$ as an abelian group in universe $u+1$. A generic fibre functor datum $F$ consists of a functor $\Phi:\mathrm{Lisse}_A(X)\to\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathrm{cont}}_A(G)$ and, for every $L$, an additive equivalence $s_L:V(\Phi L)\simeq\operatorname{geometricSections}(L)$. Define $F.\operatorname{IsNormalized}$ to mean that $\Phi$ is fully faithful and additive and has all of the following normalizations. For every $L$, $a\in A$ and $v\in V(\Phi L)$, $s_L(av)$ is the action of the actual constant scalar $a$ on $s_L(v)$. For every $g\in G$, $s_L(\rho_{\Phi L}(g)v)$ is the restriction of $s_L(v)$ along the endomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}(g)$ of $U_\Omega$. For every morphism $f:L\to M$, $s_M(\Phi(f)v)=(j^*f)_{U_\Omega}(s_L(v))$. Finally for every $f:L\to M$ and $a\in A$ there exists a morphism $t:L\to M$ whose underlying map is $f$ followed by the actual constant scalar action of $a$ on $M$, and $\Phi(t)=a\Phi(f)$. This defines only the generic map, restriction module, section group, fibre-functor data and normalization predicate; it does not assert existence of a normalized datum.
